lens: What unstated assumption is load-bearing in this artefact?

tbc-r1-f1.round_2_response: accept — Open Question raised; 019 to cite 017's stub schema verbatim before its PRD closes; stub moved to scratch path.
tbc-r1-f1.round_3_assessment: The Round-2 revision is a real improvement: OQ-1 surfaces the contract, the stub is no longer broadcast through tasks.md, and codex-r1-f2's split (017 owns interim stub, 019 owns canonical + migration adapter) inverts the load-bearing direction so 019 is no longer required to read 017's schema 'unchanged'. That dissolves the original block. However, a residual unstated assumption remains: R9 says 019 'provides a migration/adapter from this stub when 019 lands' but the PRD does not name **what 017 does between ship and 019-landing if the stub schema needs to evolve**. If 017 ships, dogfood reveals the outcome enum is missing a value (e.g. `red: failed (test-runner-crash)`), and 017's R9 enum is the only documented contract — does 017 amend R9 or does the new value land as an undocumented escape hatch? The OQ frames the contract handoff to 019 but is silent on stub-evolution-before-019. This matters because the Open Question is gated on '019's PRD synthesis' which may be quarters away; 017 needs a stub-amendment doctrine in the interim. Sharpen by adding a one-line clause to OQ-1 (or R9): 'Stub schema amendments before 019 lands are owned by 017's doctrine doc; new outcome enum values land via PR to `templates/admin/tdd-discipline.md` and are reflected in R9's enum list.' This keeps the contract auditable across the gap.
tbc-r1-f1.residual_concern: R9's outcome enum is closed (`{passed, failed, skipped (config), skipped (trivial), skipped (human-led Red lane), failed (new-file-attempted)}`) — if dogfood surfaces a seventh value, where does it land? Doctrine doc + R9 enum need a named amendment path.
tbc-r1-f1.proposed_change: Append to OQ-1 or to R9: 'Pre-019 stub schema amendments (new outcome enum values, additional fields) are owned by `templates/admin/tdd-discipline.md` and require a PR that updates both the doctrine doc and R9's enum list. 019's migration adapter must handle the union of all enum values present in the doctrine doc at the time 019 lands.'

tbc-r1-f2.round_2_response: accept — R6 extended with operational definition: vitest+typecheck+lint required, merge blocked on red, binary-AC convention.
tbc-r1-f2.round_3_assessment: The revision lands cleanly. R6 now carries a concrete tripod (required CI checks, merge-block-on-red, binary-AC convention) and explicitly states the skill does NOT validate the precondition — operator self-attests, manifest records the attestation. This is the right shape: principled-but-not-policed. The unstated assumption from R1 ('operators can self-assess strong CI signal') is now made-explicit-and-honest: it IS operator trust, and the manifest captures the trust event. The Round-2 framing also threads through to R9's enum (`red: skipped (config)` is now the auditable trace of the attestation). No residual concern — the operationalisation is tight and the auditability hook is intact.
tbc-r1-f2.residual_concern: None. The opt-out is now principled (definition exists), self-attested (operator flips the flag), and auditable (manifest records the choice).

tbc-r1-f3.round_2_response: accept — AC-8 rewritten as positive-input-list assertion; Phase E.3 reviewer-dispatch input list does NOT include the per-task manifest scratch file or the cycle markers.
tbc-r1-f3.round_3_assessment: AC-8 is now testable as written. The grep test in Round-1 false-positived on Gate 5's own `manifest.md` references; the revised AC-8 uses an awk slice (`/^## Phase E/,/^## Phase F/`) and the absence-of-substring test is now scoped to specific markers (`manifest-stub|per-task manifest scratch|cycle marker|red:.*passed|green:.*passed`) that will NOT collide with Gate 5's existing manifest.md naming. The positive-input-list claim ('Phase E.3 reviewers see only: code diff, per-task plan, tasks-file entry, role definition') is the right shape — it asserts what IS in the input list rather than relying on a global string-absence test. The original load-bearing assumption (grep-on-'manifest' yields a clean signal) is correctly diagnosed and corrected. AC-8b from the original proposed_change (Phase B context-budget input list amendment) was not separately added but is functionally absorbed by R10's clearer scope statement and the scratch-path move.
tbc-r1-f3.residual_concern: Minor: AC-8's awk slice ends at `^## Phase F` — if `develop/SKILL.md` ever inserts a sub-heading between Phase E and Phase F (e.g. a 'Phase E.8 wrap-up'), the slice still works. But if Phase E's body itself ever cites `manifest-stub` legitimately (e.g. in a docstring saying 'Phase E does not read manifest-stub files'), the AC fails because the substring is present even if its semantic intent is the opposite. This is a small risk worth flagging in the doctrine doc.
tbc-r1-f3.proposed_change: Optional sharpening: add a positive-input-list assertion as a complementary AC-8b: 'Phase E.3's reviewer-dispatch payload bullets, when sliced by `awk '/Phase E\.3/,/Phase E\.[4-9]/'`, contain exactly four input categories (code diff, per-task plan, tasks-file entry, role definition) and no others.' The current AC-8 is sufficient if the doctrine doc states the exclusion intent in plain prose; the AC-8b would lock the positive shape. Acceptance does not require this sharpening — the absence-of-substring test as scoped is reasonable.

tbc-r1-f4.round_2_response: accept — AC-2 amended with grep against develop/SKILL.md prose with 10-line proximity to a verb anchor.
tbc-r1-f4.round_3_assessment: The verb-anchor pin is the right disambiguation. AC-2's revised grep (`grep -B 0 -A 10 -E '\b(invoke|fire|run|execute)\b' ... | grep -qE 'specflow:test \{NNN-slug\} --plan-only --task T\{N\}'`) ties the literal placeholder string to a semantic context (a verb that means 'this is the actual invocation point') rather than allowing trivial satisfaction by mentioning the bash line in passing prose. The original ambiguity (template literal vs runtime trace) is now resolved: the AC is unambiguously a grep against the SKILL.md template prose, AND the proximity-to-verb-anchor constraint ensures the mention is at the actual invocation point, not in a casual reference. This is the simpler-and-tighter resolution; runtime-fixture verification (Option B in R1) would be over-engineering at PRD gate.
tbc-r1-f4.residual_concern: Minor: the regex `\b(invoke|fire|run|execute)\b` is English-prose-anchored. If the SKILL.md uses imperative voice without one of those verbs (e.g. 'The Red sub-step calls specflow:test ...'), the AC fails. 'call' is a plausible synonym worth including.
tbc-r1-f4.proposed_change: Optional: extend the verb-anchor regex to `\b(invoke|fire|run|execute|call|calls)\b` to absorb 'call' as a synonym. Acceptance does not require this — the current verb list is reasonable, and the SKILL.md author can phrase the line accordingly.

tbc-r1-f5.round_2_response: accept — R8 amended: --task T{N} mode skips Phase B.5 (Codex pass + user prompt). Per-task slice inherits the feature-level B.5 outcome; Gate 5's Codex reviewer covers cross-provider concerns.
tbc-r1-f5.round_3_assessment: The revision is the cleanest of the three resolution options the Round-1 finding offered (Option B). R8 now explicitly states `--task T{N}` mode SKIPS Phase B.5, which means the Red sub-step inside develop's single-context-window does NOT inherit a synchronous user prompt from test/SKILL.md's feature-level adversarial pass. The 029 single-context-per-task contract is preserved. Gate 5's Codex reviewer (Phase E) is the right place for cross-provider concerns at code-vs-plan time — that gate already exists and was not load-bearing for this concern. The R8 amendment also threads through to AC-6, which now greps for `Phase B\.5.*skip` — the skip is verifiable in test/SKILL.md prose. The original load-bearing assumption (synchronous external-skill prompts inside develop's window are addressed) is now made-explicit-and-resolved: they are not addressed because the prompt is skipped in `--task` mode.
tbc-r1-f5.residual_concern: One small unstated assumption persists: R8 says the per-task slice 'inherits whatever B.5 outcome the feature-level test plan recorded'. This assumes a feature-level B.5 pass HAS run before the per-task invocation — i.e. the engineer ran `specflow:test {NNN-slug} --plan-only` (no `--task` flag) at the feature level once, fielded the Codex pass + continue/revise/skip prompt, and the outcome is captured somewhere accessible to the per-task slice. If the engineer skips straight to `specflow:test {NNN-slug} --plan-only --task T1` without the feature-level pass, the per-task slice has nothing to inherit. The PRD does not state whether feature-level B.5 is a precondition of `--task` mode or whether the skip is unconditional. This is a small but load-bearing assumption for the inheritance claim to hold.
tbc-r1-f5.proposed_change: Optional sharpening: add a one-line clause to R8: 'When `--task T{N}` is supplied, Phase B.5 is skipped regardless of whether a feature-level B.5 outcome exists. The inheritance phrasing is honest about the audit trail (the feature-level outcome, if any, is the only B.5 record); when no feature-level outcome exists, the per-task invocation simply has no B.5 trace and Gate 5's Codex reviewer is the sole adversarial pass.' This makes the precondition explicit. Acceptance does not require this — the revision is sufficient as-is and the precondition can land in the doctrine doc rather than the PRD.

summary: Round 2 accepted all five Round-1 findings and the revisions are sound. tbc-r1-f2, tbc-r1-f3, tbc-r1-f4, tbc-r1-f5 are accepted with minor optional sharpenings (synonym extensions, positive-shape complementary ACs, precondition clarifications) — none of these residuals are blocking. tbc-r1-f1 is sharpened: the 017→019 absorption contract is now correctly inverted (017 owns interim stub, 019 owns canonical + migration adapter, OQ-1 surfaces the handoff), but a residual unstated assumption remains around stub-schema-evolution-before-019. If dogfood surfaces a new outcome enum value before 019 lands, the PRD does not name the amendment path — recommend adding a one-line clause to OQ-1 or R9 stating that pre-019 stub amendments land via PR to `templates/admin/tdd-discipline.md` with R9's enum list updated in lockstep. Net: PRD is gate-ready; one optional doctrine-doc sharpening recommended for stub evolution governance.
principle_pulse: Think Before Coding asks: what unstated assumption is load-bearing? Round 2 surfaced four of five hidden assumptions explicitly (CI signal definition, Phase E input list, AC-2 verification mechanism, B.5 prompt collision) and inverted the fifth (017→019 schema ownership flipped from 'fixed contract' to 'interim stub + 019 adapter'). The remaining residual — stub-schema-evolution-before-019 — is a smaller load-bearing assumption hidden inside the inversion's success.
